claim: GTPases of the Ras superfamily regulate cell growth, membrane traffic and the cytoskeleton.
source: The GTPases of the Ras superfamily regulate cell growth, membrane traffic and the cytoskeleton, and a wide range of diseases are caused by mutations in particular members.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about Ras superfamily GTPases, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: A wide range of diseases are caused by mutations in particular members of the Ras superfamily.
source: The GTPases of the Ras superfamily regulate cell growth, membrane traffic and the cytoskeleton, and a wide range of diseases are caused by mutations in particular members.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the introduction discussing disease-causing mutations.

claim: Active GTP-bound GTPases recruit a specific set of effector proteins to the membrane.
source: They function as switchable landmarks with the active GTP-bound form recruiting to the membrane a specific set of effector proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GTPase function, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: GTPases are controlled by regulators that promote acquisition of GTP (GEFs) or its hydrolysis to GDP (GAPs).
source: The GTPases are precisely controlled by regulators that promote acquisition of GTP (GEFs) or its hydrolysis to GDP (GAPs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GTPase regulation, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: MitoID is a method for identifying effectors and regulators by performing in vivo proximity biotinylation with mitochondrially-localized forms of GTPases.
source: We report here MitoID, a method for identifying effectors and regulators by performing in vivo proximity biotinylation with mitochondrially-localized forms of the GTPases.
evidence: This is the primary methodological claim of the paper, supported by the experimental data presented throughout.

claim: Applying MitoID to 11 human Rab GTPases identified many known effectors and GAPs.
source: Applying this to 11 human Rab GTPases identified many known effectors and GAPs, as well as putative novel effectors, with examples of the latter validated for Rab2, Rab5, Rab9 and Rab11.
evidence: This claim is supported by the mass spectrometry data and analysis presented in the results section.

claim: MitoID identified putative novel effectors for Rab2, Rab5, Rab9 and Rab11 that were validated.
source: Applying this to 11 human Rab GTPases identified many known effectors and GAPs, as well as putative novel effectors, with examples of the latter validated for Rab2, Rab5, Rab9 and Rab11.
evidence: This claim is supported by validation experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: MitoID can efficiently identify effectors and GAPs of Rho and Ras family GTPases such as Cdc42, RhoA, Rheb, and N-Ras.
source: MitoID can also efficiently identify effectors and GAPs of Rho and Ras family GTPases such as Cdc42, RhoA, Rheb, and N-Ras, and can identify GEFs by use of GDP-bound forms.
evidence: This claim is supported by the mass spectrometry data presented in Figures 8 and 9.

claim: MitoID can identify GEFs by use of GDP-bound forms of GTPases.
source: MitoID can also efficiently identify effectors and GAPs of Rho and Ras family GTPases such as Cdc42, RhoA, Rheb, and N-Ras, and can identify GEFs by use of GDP-bound forms.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing GEF identification with GDP-locked forms in Figures 6, 8, and 9.

claim: Small GTPases share a similar nucleotide-binding fold with surface loops arranged differently depending on whether GTP or GDP is bound.
source: These proteins share a similar nucleotide-binding fold, with the arrangement of surface loops altered depending on whether GTP or GDP is bound (Vetter and Wittinghofer, 2001).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Small GTPases typically lack intrinsic GTPase activity.
source: Although often called GTPases, they typically lack intrinsic GTPase activity and instead nucleotide status is determined by regulatory proteins that either stimulate GTP hydrolysis, or exchange GDP for GTP (Müller and Goody, 2018; Barr and Lambright, 2010; Cherfils and Zeghouf, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GTPase biochemistry supported by citations.

claim: G proteins generally only bind their effectors when in the GTP-bound state.
source: This allows the G protein's binding interactions to be regulated and hence they act as molecular switches that generally only bind their effectors when in the GTP-bound state.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GTPase function.

claim: The two main approaches for finding effectors have been yeast two-hybrid screens and affinity chromatography.

claim: Both yeast two-hybrid and affinity chromatography approaches take advantage of mutations that lock the G protein in an active or inactive conformation.
source: Both take advantage of mutations that in many members of the family lock the G protein in an active or inactive conformation (Vetter and Wittinghofer, 2001; Itzen and Goody, 2011; Feig, 1999; Der et al., 1986).

evidence: This is a statement about capabilities and limitations of affinity chromatography based on knowledge of the technique.

claim: Affinity chromatography requires production of correctly folded GTPase and typically requires large amounts of cell lysate.
source: The affinity chromatography approach can detect binding to protein complexes, but requires production of correctly folded GTPase, and typically requires large amounts of cell lysate, and interactors have to bind tightly enough to persist during the column washing that is required to remove the rest of the cell lysate before the interactors are eluted and identified.

claim: Proximity biotinylation has emerged as a new approach for identifying protein-protein interactions.
source: Recently, proximity biotinylation has emerged as a new approach for identifying protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is a statement about recent methodological developments.

claim: If a protein is expressed as a fusion to a promiscuous biotin ligase (BioID) or engineered peroxidase (APEX), proteins in the vicinity become biotinylated and can be isolated with streptavidin.
source: If a protein of interest is expressed in cells as a fusion to a promiscuous biotin ligase (BioID) or an engineered peroxidase (APEX) then proteins in the vicinity become biotinylated and can be isolated with streptavidin and identified by mass-spectrometry (Roux et al., 2012; Martell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about proximity biotinylation methods supported by citations.

claim: Applying proximity biotinylation to small GTPases is potentially problematic since the fusion must not interfere with effector binding or membrane targeting.
source: However, applying this to small GTPases is potentially problematic since the fusion to the protein that generates biotin must not interfere with effector binding or membrane targeting.
evidence: This is a logical inference about potential challenges in applying the method.

claim: To distinguish specific interactors from bystanders, it is important to compare several different fusion proteins that have a similar location.
source: In addition, in order to distinguish specific interactors from those biotinylated because they simply happen to be in the same location it is important to compare several different fusion proteins that have a similar location, and yet different GTPases typically act on different membranes making direct comparison more challenging.

claim: Different GTPases typically act on different membranes making direct comparison more challenging.

claim: GDP-bound forms of GTPases are generally not membrane bound and will have a different background set of bystanders to the GTP-bound form.
source: In addition, the GDP-bound forms that are used as a control in yeast two-hybrid and affinity chromatography are generally not membrane bound and so will have a different background set of bystanders to the GTP-bound form.

source: We find that in this ectopic location there is a similar set of background interactions, but each G protein also interacts with specific effectors and regulators which can be readily identified by comparative analysis.

source: We find that in this ectopic location there is a similar set of background interactions, but each G protein also interacts with specific effectors and regulators which can be readily identified by comparative analysis.

source: Mitochondria have proven useful for ectopic relocation of cytosolic proteins as there are well defined targeting signals for inserting proteins into the outer membrane of mitochondria without interfering with mitochondrial function (Silvius et al., 2006; Mitoma and Ito, 1992; Hoogenraad et al., 2003).

claim: The position of BirA* is close enough to the switch regions to modify effectors without interfering with their binding.
source: The BirA* biotin ligase was placed after the C-terminal unstructured linker of the GTPase but before the mitochondrial transmembrane domain, a position close enough to the switch regions to modify effectors without interfering with their binding.

claim: The Q79L mutation locks Rab5A into the GTP-bound form by blocking GAP activity.
source: Rab5A was expressed with single residue changes that are known to lock it into either the GTP-bound form by blocking GAP activity (Q79L) or the GDP-bound form by interfering with GTP binding (S34N) (Li and Stahl, 1993; Stenmark et al., 1994).

source: Rab5A was expressed with single residue changes that are known to lock it into either the GTP-bound form by blocking GAP activity (Q79L) or the GDP-bound form by interfering with GTP binding (S34N) (Li and Stahl, 1993; Stenmark et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Rab5A chimeras accumulated on mitochondria when expressed in cells.

claim: Probing with streptavidin revealed accumulation of biotin on mitochondria indicating that the BirA* part of the chimera had retained activity.

claim: Biotinylation of endosomal proteins should reflect an interaction with Rab5 and not an altered location of their organelle of residence.
source: The presence of Rab5A on mitochondria did not result in the wholesale relocation of endosomes to the mitochondrial surface, and hence biotinylation of endosomal proteins should reflect an interaction with Rab5 and not an altered location of their organelle of residence (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).

claim: Rab2A chimeras accumulated on mitochondria but did not cause gross relocation of the Golgi.

evidence: This is directly observed in the immunofluorescence images in Figure 1E,F.

claim: MitoID with GTP-bound Rab5A biotinylated approximately 20 proteins known to bind directly to Rab5-GTP or to be subunits of complexes that bind to Rab5-GTP.
source: Examining the proteins with lower counts revealed that ~ 20 proteins known to bind directly to Rab5-GTP, or to be subunits of complexes that bind to Rab5-GTP, where found to be biotinylated specifically by the GTP-bound form (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Canonical Rab5 effectors such as EEA1, Huntingtin and Rabenosyn-5 were biotinylated by GTP-bound Rab5A.
source: These include canonical Rab5 effectors such as EEA1, Huntingtin and Rabenosyn-5; as well as subunits of complexes that bind Rab5 such as CORVET, class III PI 3-kinase, and FTS/Hook/p107FHIP (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Xu et al., 2008; Simonsen et al., 1998; Nielsen et al., 2000; Christoforidis et al., 1999b).

source: These include canonical Rab5 effectors such as EEA1, Huntingtin and Rabenosyn-5; as well as subunits of complexes that bind Rab5 such as CORVET, class III PI 3-kinase, and FTS/Hook/p107FHIP (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Xu et al., 2008; Simonsen et al., 1998; Nielsen et al., 2000; Christoforidis et al., 1999b).

claim: Rabex-5 forms a complex with Rabaptin-5, an effector for Rab5A, an interaction thought to amplify Rab5 activation.
source: The third GEF, Rabex-5, was found at similar levels with both Rab5A mutants, but it is known to form a complex with Rabaptin-5, an effector for Rab5A, an interaction thought to amplify Rab5 activation (Horiuchi et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Almost all known Rab5 effectors and GEFs were detected in all three biological replicates.

claim: The detection of known Rab5 effectors and GEFs in all three replicates indicates that the approach is robust and reproducible.

claim: When Rab5A is fused to BirA* and relocated to mitochondria it is still able to bind effectors and regulatory proteins in a nucleotide-specific manner.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that when Rab5A is fused to BirA* and relocated to the surface of mitochondria it is still able to bind effectors and regulatory proteins in a nucleotide-specific manner.

source: More importantly, these interactions are stable enough for the interaction partners to become biotinylated by BirA* and hence identified by BioID.

source: However, Rab5 is one of the most abundant small GTPases in cultured cells, suggesting that its interactors may also be relatively abundant.

claim: MitoID was applied to a panel of sixteen additional small GTPases including ten Rab GTPases and six from the Rho and Ras families.
source: To determine if the MitoID approach is broadly effective for small GTPases we applied it to a panel of sixteen other small GTPases. These include ten further Rab GTPases: Rab2A, Rab6A, Rab18, Rab30 and Rab33B from the Golgi, Rab8A and Rab10 from post-Golgi carriers, Rab11A from recycling endosomes and Rab7A and Rab9A from late endosomes (Hutagalung and Novick, 2011). In addition, we examined Cdc42, Rac1 and RhoA from the Rho family and Rheb, RalA and N-Ras from the Ras family.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: All sixteen GTPases were expressed as fusions to mitochondrial BirA* with residue changes known or predicted to lock them in the GTP-bound or GDP-bound states.

claim: All of the GTPase chimeras accumulated on mitochondria.

claim: Targeting GTPase chimeras to mitochondria does not induce mitochondrial stress.

claim: Comparing results from one bait to many other baits increases the sensitivity and accuracy with which true interaction partners can be distinguished from non-specific background.

evidence: This is established knowledge about proteomics data analysis supported by citations.

claim: The CompPASS platform uses spectral counts and converts these to a D-score.
source: The CompPASS platform uses spectral counts and converts these to a 'D-score' by dividing the spectral counts for each protein by the number of baits for which the protein was a hit, and then raising it to the power of the number of times it was replicated with a given bait (Sowa et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a description of an established analysis method supported by citation.

claim: Proteins that are found with all replicates of one bait but not with any other bait have the highest D scores.
source: Thus, proteins that are found with all replicates of one bait, but not found with any other bait, have the highest D scores.
evidence: This is an explanation of how the D-score works.

claim: The WD variant of the D-score gives extra weight to interactions where several baits show significantly higher spectral counts than the mean obtained with all the baits.
source: Thus for the D-score we used the WD variant that gives extra weight to interactions where several baits show significantly higher spectral counts than the mean obtained with all the baits (Behrends et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a description of the analysis method used, supported by citation.

claim: For volcano plots, each GTP-bound form was compared to all GDP-bound forms on the grounds that effectors generally do not bind to the GDP-form.

evidence: This is a description of the analysis strategy based on known GTPase biology.

claim: GDP-forms were compared to all other GDP-bound forms as it is unlikely that exchange factors act on more than one or two specific GTPases.

source: The top ten most significant hits with the GTP form of RalB include six subunits of the exocyst vesicle tethering complex, a known RalB effector, including the EXOC2/Sec5 subunit to which RalB binds directly (Sugihara et al., 2002) (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 8C and supported by citation.

claim: The hits with RalB also include the Ral effector RLIP/RalBP1 and its binding partner REPS1/Reps1, and the subunits of the two known Ral GAPs.
source: The hits also include the Ral effector RLIP/RalBP1 and its binding partner REPS1/Reps1, and the subunits of the two known Ral GAPs (RALGAPA1/2 and RALGAPB) (Yamaguchi et al., 1997; Shirakawa et al., 2009).
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data and supported by citations.

claim: The top hit with the GTP-bound form of Rheb is the mTORC1 subunit Raptor that is located next to the Rheb binding site on mTor.
source: The top hit with the GTP-bound form of Rheb is the mTORC1 subunit Raptor that is located next to the Rheb binding site on mTor (Yang et al., 2017) (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 8D and supported by citation.

claim: The next two hits with Rheb are Tsc1 and Tsc2, the subunits of the Rheb GAP that controls the activity of Rheb and hence mTORC1.
source: The next two hits are Tsc1 and Tsc2, the subunits of the Rheb GAP that controls the activity of Rheb and hence mTORC1 (Manning and Cantley, 2003).
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data and supported by citation.

claim: The top 25 most significant hits with the GTP-form of Cdc42 include 19 known Cdc42 effectors, two known Cdc42 GAPs (ARHGAP31/32), and myosin18A.
source: The top 25 most significant hits with the GTP-form of Cdc42 include 19 known Cdc42 effectors (including kinases, actin regulators and scaffolding proteins), two known Cdc42 GAPs (ARHGAP31/32), and myosin18A that has been reported to form a complex with CDC42BPB, one of the Cdc42 effectors (Tan et al., 2008; Vigil et al., 2010) (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9A and supported by citations.

claim: With the GDP-locked form of Cdc42 the top hits include four members of the DOCK family of Rho GEFs that are known to activate Cdc42.
source: With the GDP-locked form of Cdc42 the top hits include four members of the DOCK family of Rho GEFs that are known to activate Cdc42, along with LRCH2 and LRCH3 that have recently been found to interact with a subset of DOCK family GEFs (O'Loughlin et al., 2018) (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9B and supported by citation.

claim: The top 35 hits with GTP-locked RhoA include 19 known effectors including kinases, scaffolds, RhoA GEFs, and phosphatases.
source: The top 35 hits with GTP-locked RhoA include 19 known effectors including kinases like PKN1 and CIT/Citron, scaffolds like the Rhotekins RTKN/RTKN2, RhoA GEFs such as ARHGEF1/p115-RhoAGEF and ARHGEF12, and phosphatases such as INPPL1/SHIP (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: There are six known RhoA GAPs among the hits with GTP-locked RhoA such as ABR, ARHGAP5, ARHGAP35/p190RhoGAP.
source: In addition, there are six known RhoA GAPs such as ABR, ARHGAP5, ARHGAP35/p190RhoGAP.
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: With the GDP-locked form of RhoA the top four hits are all known RhoA GEFs.
source: With the GDP-locked form of RhoA the top four hits are all known RhoA GEFs, with further other GEFs with lesser scores (Figure 9D).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: The top four RhoA GEFs were also hits with the GTP-form of RhoA reflecting the fact that they are also effectors that act in a positive feedback loop.
source: The top four were also hits mentioned above with the GTP-form of RhoA reflecting the fact that they are also effectors that act in a positive feedback loop (Medina et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an explanation of the observation supported by citation.

claim: Initial application of MitoID to Rac1 revealed known interactors but also showed Rac1-specific biotinylation of many DNA or RNA binding proteins.
source: Initial application of MitoID to Rac1 revealed known interactors but also showed Rac1-specific biotinylation of many DNA or RNA binding proteins, with these interactions typically being nucleotide-state independent (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Some Ras family GTPases have poly-basic stretches next to their C-terminal lipid anchors which stabilize interactions with acidic phospholipids.
source: Some Ras family GTPases have poly-basic stretches next to their C-terminal lipid anchors which stabilize interactions with acidic phospholipids in the cytosolic leaflet of the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GTPase structure.

claim: On the neutral membranes of mitochondria, basic residues in Rac1 might recruit nucleic acids.
source: On the neutral membranes of mitochondria these basic residues might instead recruit nucleic acids and so we repeated the MitoID with Rac1 lacking the six consecutive basic residues adjacent to the lipid anchor.
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the observation of nucleic acid binding proteins.

claim: Removing the six consecutive basic residues from Rac1 reduced the number of nucleic-acid binding proteins but did not prevent interactions with effectors.
source: This reduced the number of nucleic-acid binding proteins but did not prevent interactions with effectors and so our analysis was performed with this version of Rac1 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The top eight hits with Rac1-GTP are all known Rac1 effectors.
source: The top eight hits with Rac1-GTP are all known Rac1 effectors, the GIT/PIX (ARFGEF6/7) complexes that are also Cdc42/Rac1 GEFs, the PAK2 kinase and the WASF2, ABI1 and CYFIP subunits of the WAVE2 actin regulatory complex (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: The next 30 most significant hits with Rac1-GTP include ten further Rac1 effectors and six Rac1 GAPs.
source: The next 30 most significant hits include ten further Rac1 effectors, and six Rac1 GAPs.
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: With the GDP-locked form of Rac1 the top four hits are members of the DOCK family of Rho GEFs.
source: With the GDP-locked form of Rac1 the top four hits are members of the DOCK family of Rho GEFs (Figure 9F).
evidence: This is observed in the data shown in Figure 9F.

claim: DOCK6 and DOCK7 were found with both Rac1 and Cdc42 whereas DOCKs 1,4 and 5 were specific to Rac1 and DOCKs 9 and 11 were specific to Cdc42, accurately reflecting their known substrate specificity.
source: Interestingly, DOCK6 and DOCK7 were found with both Rac1 and Cdc42 whereas DOCKs 1,4 and 5 were specific to Rac1 and DOCKs 9 and 11 were specific to Cdc42, accurately reflecting their known substrate specificity (Gadea and Blangy, 2014).
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data and supported by citation.

claim: The MitoID approach works not only with Rab GTPases but also with members of the Ras and Rho families of GTPases.
source: Taken together these results provide overwhelming evidence that the MitoID approach works not only with Rab GTPases but also with the members of the Ras and Rho families of GTPases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comprehensive data with multiple GTPase families.

claim: Relocating a set of baits to the same ectopic location can still be compatible with binding to known interactors whilst allowing meaningful comparison between baits.
source: We show here that relocating a set of baits to the same ectopic location can still be compatible with binding to known interactors whilst allowing the advantage of meaningful comparison between baits.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful application of MitoID.

claim: Expressing human proteins in cultured cells allows access to relevant chaperones or post-translational modifications, maximizing the chance that the bait is active.
source: Expressing human proteins in cultured cells allows access to relevant chaperones or post-translational modifications, maximizing the chance that the bait is active.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the advantages of the method.

claim: The binding in MitoID is assayed in living cytosol and hence at native protein and ion concentrations.
source: The binding is assayed in living cytosol and hence at native protein and ion concentrations.
evidence: This is a description of a methodological advantage.

claim: Over-expression in MitoID should increase the biotinylation of targets without the risk of accumulation in an undesired location.
source: As the protein is at an ectopic location with a large capacity to handle exogenous proteins then over-expression should increase the biotinylation of targets without the risk of accumulation in an undesired location.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the advantages of the method.

claim: MitoID does not require a very large number of cells.
source: Finally, it should be noted that the method does not require a very large number of cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the practical requirements of the method.

claim: For each MitoID replicate, two T175 flasks totalling 5 × 10^7 cells were used.
source: For each replicate we used two T175 flasks totalling 5 × 107 cells that were transiently transfected with the expression plasmid, and so MitoID should be readily applicable to comparing different cell types.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental conditions used.

claim: For Rab5 there are 16 reported mammalian effector proteins or complexes that are conserved in Drosophila, of which 14 were found by MitoID and 13 by affinity chromatography of S2 lysate.
source: For Rab5 there are 16 reported mammalian effector proteins or complexes that are conserved in Drosophila, of which 14 were found by MitoID and 13 by affinity chromatography of S2 lysate (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a comparison of methods based on data in Supplementary file 5.

claim: MitoID found all three reported Rab5 effectors that are not conserved in flies.
source: MitoID also found all three of the reported effectors that are not conserved in flies.
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: For Rab2 there are 12 reported mammalian effector proteins or complexes that are conserved in Drosophila, of which 11 were found by MitoID and eight by affinity chromatography of S2 cell lysate.
source: For Rab2 there are 12 reported mammalian effector proteins or complexes that are conserved in Drosophila, of which 11 were found by MitoID and eight by affinity chromatography of S2 cell lysate (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a comparison of methods based on data in Supplementary file 5.

claim: MitoID can perform as well, if not better, than affinity chromatography.
source: Taken together, this analysis indicates that the MitoID can perform as well, if not better, than affinity chromatography, and illustrates MitoID's ability to find novel effectors for even well characterized Rabs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison with affinity chromatography.

claim: It is possible that some GTPase effectors will require a specific lipid for stable membrane association.
source: Firstly, it is possible that some GTPase effectors will require a specific lipid for stable membrane association, although we were able to find binding partners for GTPases from several different locations that are known to differ in lipid composition.
evidence: This is a statement about a potential limitation with a counterargument based on the data.

claim: It may be harder to detect GTPase effectors that are normally present on mitochondria.
source: Secondly, it may be harder to detect GTPase effectors that are normally present on mitochondria.
evidence: This is a statement about a potential limitation.

claim: TBC1D15 and Vps13C were detected on the bubble-volcano plots as putative hits with Rab5 and Rab7 respectively, albeit with low WD scores.
source: The Rab5 effector TBC1D15 and the Rab7 effector Vps13C are known to be associated with mitochondria, and indeed were biotinylated by most of the baits. However, they were also detected on the bubble-volcano plots as putative hits with Rab5 and Rab7 respectively, albeit with low WD scores, indicating that at least in these two cases the extra degree of biotinylation allowed them to emerge from the mitochondrial background.
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: Known GEFs were only found with a subset of the Rab GTPases.
source: Thirdly, we only found known GEFs with a subset of the Rab GTPases.
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: The canonical 'GDP-locked' mutation has a complex effect in that it destabilizes the binding of both GTP and GDP but the latter interaction is less affected.
source: This may reflect the fact that the canonical 'GDP-locked' mutation used in this study has a complex effect in that it destabilizes the binding of both GTP and GDP but the latter interaction is less affected in the limited number of cases examined (Koch et al., 2016; John et al., 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The precise details of GTPase structure and activation cycle are somewhat variable.
source: Although all Ras superfamily members share the same general fold it is known that the precise details of their structure and activation cycle are somewhat variable (Langemeyer et al., 2014; Merithew et al., 2001; Cherfils and Zeghouf, 2013; Eathiraj et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The GDP-locked form of Rab27A is rapidly degraded in vivo suggesting that the mutation destabilizes the protein.
source: It has been reported that the GDP-locked form of Rab27A is rapidly degraded in vivo suggesting that the mutation destabilizes the protein, and here we found that GDP forms of Rab7A and Rab18 were expressed at lower levels and did not detect their GEFs (Ramalho et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement about known behavior supported by citation and confirmed by data in this study.

claim: Successful application of MitoID with the GDP-locked form requires that the empty state is stable and able to bind the GEF sufficiently tightly to allow detection.
source: It may thus be that successful application of MitoID with the GDP-locked form requires that the empty state is not only stable but also able to bind the GEF sufficiently tightly to allow detection, and it is possible that screening further mutations in the nucleotide binding pocket could facilitate this.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the requirements for successful GEF detection.

claim: Known effectors were found with all of the non-Rab GTPases examined.
source: Fourthly, although we found known effectors with all of the non-Rab GTPases examined, we did not find high confidence hits with a few Rabs that we tested including Rab7L1, Rab19, and Rab39 and so they were not included in the analysis.
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: High confidence hits were not found with Rab7L1, Rab19, and Rab39.
source: Fourthly, although we found known effectors with all of the non-Rab GTPases examined, we did not find high confidence hits with a few Rabs that we tested including Rab7L1, Rab19, and Rab39 and so they were not included in the analysis.
evidence: This is observed in the mass spectrometry data.

claim: Rab7L1, Rab19, and Rab39 are known to be much less abundant in HeLa cells than the Rabs presented in the study.
source: These Rabs are known to be much less abundant in HeLa cells than the Rabs presented here and so it is possible that their effectors are too scarce to be detected with the conditions used (Hein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about known abundance supported by citation.

claim: More active variants of BirA* have been recently reported.
source: Our approach relied on using the original BirA* biotin ligase but more active variants have been recently reported (Branon et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about recent methodological developments supported by citations.

claim: The sensitivity of mass-spectrometers is still increasing.
source: Likewise, the sensitivity of mass-spectrometers is still increasing.
evidence: This is a statement about ongoing technological improvements.

claim: Exploring more mutations in the GTPases may identify GTP-locked or GDP-bound/empty forms that act more effectively to capture effectors or GEFs respectively.
source: Finally, exploring more mutations in the GTPases may identify GTP-locked or GDP-bound/empty forms that act more effectively to capture effectors or GEFs respectively.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future improvements based on logical reasoning.

claim: MitoID allows rapid testing of sequence variants by transient transfection followed by streptavidin isolation and immunoblotting for known interactors.
source: Indeed, MitoID allows rapid testing of sequence variants - following transient transfection of variants, the biotinylated proteins can be isolated with streptavidin and probed by immunoblotting for known interactors.
evidence: This is a description of a methodological capability.

claim: Mutating Ser84 in Rab5A to alanine or glutamate greatly reduced biotinylation of OSBPL9 but not other effectors.
source: To illustrate this we tested the effect on Rab5A-GTP of mutations in Ser84 that has been identified as a potential site for phosphorylation (Steger et al., 2017; Ong et al., 2014). Mutating this to alanine or glutamate greatly reduced biotinylation of one effector (OSBPL9), but not others, suggesting that modification of this residue could differentially affect effector binding (Figure 9—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is observed in the immunoblot data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1C and supported by citations.

claim: Modification of Ser84 in Rab5A could differentially affect effector binding.
source: Mutating this to alanine or glutamate greatly reduced biotinylation of one effector (OSBPL9), but not others, suggesting that modification of this residue could differentially affect effector binding (Figure 9—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects observed in the immunoblot.

claim: The MitoID approach and the data presented will be of help to many labs investigating small GTPases and potentially other families of proteins that function through transient interactions with cytosolic proteins.
source: We anticipate that the MitoID approach, and the data presented in this paper, will be of help to many labs investigating small GTPases and potentially other families of proteins that function through transient interactions with cytosolic proteins.
evidence: This is a statement about the anticipated impact of the work.
